title: IPL photofacial
caption: An IPL photofacial uses broad-spectrum light — not a single focused laser beam — to target multiple skin concerns at once: pigmentation, redness, and uneven tone. The light energy is absorbed by melanin and haemoglobin, which breaks down discolouration and calms visible vessels without removing the skin's surface. Because it works beneath the skin, there's no open wound — but redness and darkening of spots for a few days is normal. Knowing that it's a light device, not a laser, and that it targets colour in the skin changes how you read any IPL before-and-after. Not medical advice, just the honest basics.
